words.gloss_range: completed reported saying that opens a direct rebuking quotation
words.root_gloss_range: uttered speech, declaration, report, and proposition; locally selected as outward reported speech with self-citation force
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) makes the whole ayah a reported speech event before the rebuke itself begins, not a narrative explanation of the ship breach. Its active perfect form keeps the speaker responsible but unnamed, so the response is compact and authoritative. The word also starts the recursion of the scene: present speech introduces a question about prior speech, placing this first rebuke within the repeated warning sequence at 18:67, 18:72, 18:75, and 18:78, before the later repetition adds a separate dative address.

topics.headline: outer speech verb turns the ayah into quoted rebuke
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from the ship incident into a single direct-speech domain rather than a narrative explanation.
topics.reason: The attachment data makes the following rhetorical question the quoted complement of the speech verb, while the local direct quote selects outward articulation from the speech root.

topics.headline: active perfect reports the speaker compactly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the responsible speaker is carried by active perfect morphology and context, so the rebuke begins compactly without renaming him.
topics.reason: QAC gives a 3ms active perfect with no overt subject; attachment evidence treats the subject as morphologically present and contextually recoverable.

topics.headline: speech root launches the warning refrain recursion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that speech introduces speech about prior speech, and that this first rebuke belongs to the escalating warning refrain at 18:67, 18:72, 18:75, and 18:78.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah anchors, and the local structure repeats the speech root in the outer report and embedded self-citation.

words.gloss_range: rhetorical past-negating question particle that governs the following cited saying
words.prose: {{ar:أَلَمْ}} ({{tr:alam}}) fuses question and negation into a rebuking operator. It governs the following cited saying as a jussive, so the force is closer to "did I not already say?" than to a neutral question. In the dialogue movement, this word turns the warning of 18:67 into the first post-failure reproach, creating the pressure that 18:73 answers with apology.

topics.headline: negative question becomes a rebuking acknowledgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form is not a request for information; it presses Musa to acknowledge what had already been said.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the interrogative plus jussive-particle combination and attachment support marks the utterance as a rhetorical question with rebuking force.

topics.headline: question frame converts prediction into reproach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the earlier warning from 18:67 returns with a new speech-act frame: prediction has become compelled acknowledgment.
topics.reason: The local particle frame governs the following saying verb, and the CRITICAL rows tie the resulting formula to the first reproach after 18:67.

words.gloss_range: first-person jussive saying used as self-citation of a prior warning
words.root_gloss_range: uttered speech, saying, proposition, and citation; locally narrowed to a remembered statement used as evidence
words.prose: {{ar:أَقُلْ}} ({{tr:aqul}}) is the self-citing center of the rebuke. Its first-person form keeps the speaker inside the verb, while jussive governance makes the saying a past-cited warning rather than a live present assertion. The speech act both reports and performs correction: al-Khiḍr cites what he had said, and Musa's interruption has just made the warning usable as evidence. The formula also sits beside authority-vindication scenes (2:33; 12:96), while 18:14 remains an opposite-valence speech contrast, and it belongs to the local escalation from 18:67 to 18:75 and 18:78.

topics.headline: first-person jussive marks prior self-citation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker is encoded in the verb while its shortened jussive form makes the saying a recalled prior claim, not a fresh present assertion.
topics.reason: The following content clause is governed by the verb, while the preceding particle accounts for the jussive, past-negated force.

topics.headline: saying performs the rebuke it reports
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cited saying functions as evidence: the rebuke is built from a prior statement whose truth Musa has just demonstrated.
topics.reason: The q-w-l range supports uttered statement and proposition, and the local syntax embeds the warning as the content now cited.

topics.headline: authority-vindication parallels clarify the formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the formula resembles other scenes where a knower cites prior speech after confirmation (2:33; 12:96), while 18:14 supplies an opposite-valence speech contrast rather than controlling this local parse.
topics.reason: The concrete parallels survive as formulaic comparison and contrast; local grammar still selects al-Khiḍr citing his own warning in this dialogue.

topics.headline: middle speech layer creates recursive warning structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the middle layer of speech-within-speech, where the same speech root turns the ayah back toward the warning sequence at 18:67, 18:72, 18:75, and 18:78.
topics.reason: The verb stands between the narrator-reported speech and the embedded assertion, and the CRITICAL rows preserve the same-surah escalation and root reprise.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle plus second-person suffix opening a direct asserted diagnosis
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّكَ}} ({{tr:innaka}}) begins the recalled warning as a certainty claim. The attached second-person suffix places Musa inside that assertion as the one whose capacity is about to be denied, keeping the rebuke direct without adding a separate name. Because this same content opening returns from 18:67 and is sharpened later in 18:75, the word carries both personal targeting and refrain recognition. Its nasal close also leads into the following negator, making assertion and negation audibly linked without changing the syntax.

topics.headline: emphatic particle scopes over the inability claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted content begins as a formally asserted diagnosis, not as a tentative comment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the particle open the content clause and links the following negated capacity predicate as its report.

topics.headline: attached pronoun places Musa inside the assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressee is not named externally; he is grammatically inserted as the bearer of the asserted incapacity.
topics.reason: The suffix is the governed subject of the particle and is identified by attachment evidence as the addressed interlocutor.

topics.headline: opening of the warning formula returns before sharper address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the content opening repeats the warning from 18:67 and precedes the sharper later form in 18:75, where the address expands.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give 18:67 and 18:75 as concrete anchors, and attachment support marks the content as the repeated patience-warning refrain.

topics.headline: sound binds assertion to negation without changing syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible binding between assertion and negation, while the syntactic force still comes from the particle and following negator.
topics.reason: The prosodic row survives as sound texture; local syntax, not sound, governs the predicate relationship.

words.gloss_range: future-oriented negator governing the following capacity verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَنْ}} ({{tr:lan}}) turns the emphatic address into a denied-capacity predicate. It governs the following verb, so the inability is built into the grammar of the warning. The particle can carry categorical pressure, but here that force is best kept within the repeated companionship test: prediction in 18:67, rebuke in 18:72 and 18:75, and demonstrated non-endurance in 18:78. It also answers the prior emphatic judgment about the act with an emphatic incapacity judgment about the observer.

topics.headline: future negator governs the capacity verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that incapacity is grammatically locked onto the following verb, not merely inferred from the story.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as governing subjunctive mood on the capacity verb, and attachment evidence places that verb in the predicate of the assertion.

topics.headline: future denial carries debated categorical pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation can feel categorical within the episode, while the classical permanence debate should not be overstated as an unlimited metaphysical claim.
topics.reason: The source rows explicitly note the debate; the local context supports decisive future denial of capacity with al-Khiḍr, not an unqualified claim about every possible setting.

topics.headline: same negator grows heavier through repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated negator moving from prediction (18:67) to reminder (18:72) to escalation (18:75), before completed non-endurance appears in 18:78.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide the concrete same-surah sequence, and local grammar confirms the same negated capacity formula in this ayah.

words.gloss_range: negated internal capacity for sustaining patience in the speaker-bound companionship setting
words.root_gloss_range: willing compliance, tractability, and practical capacity; locally narrowed to Form X ability sought within oneself rather than bare obedience or voluntary initiative
words.prose: {{ar:تَسْتَطِيعَ}} ({{tr:tastaṭīʿa}}) is the predicate core of the warning. It is not loose ability: the following companionship phrase sets the condition and the final patience noun names the domain of failure. The Form X shape lets the ability carry willingness and self-tractability pressure, so Musa is not simply weak in power; he cannot find within himself the capacity for restraint with al-Khiḍr. Its second-person prefix keeps the same addressee carried from the emphatic pronoun, now under the negator's subjunctive control. The fuller verb also belongs to the repeated warning stages at 18:67, 18:72, and 18:75 before the contracted resolution in 18:78.

topics.headline: capacity verb takes companionship condition and patience object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is not generic ability; it is immediately specified by a companionship condition and by patience as the domain of failure.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the verb to the adverbial companion phrase and to the explicit patience complement.

topics.headline: Form X makes ability feel internally sought and willingness-colored
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the inability involves finding tractable self-capacity for restraint, while local usage still selects ability rather than simple obedience or volunteered action.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports willingness and compliance pressure, but the local Form X capacity verb and patience complement keep the selected sense as internal ability for restraint.

topics.headline: second-person subjunctive carries addressee continuity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same addressed person carried from the emphatic pronoun into the verb, now under negated subjunctive control.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as second masculine singular and subjunctive under the negator, with the subject morphologically present.

topics.headline: capacity verb repeats until the later contracted resolution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fuller repeated capacity form belongs to the warning stages at 18:67, 18:72, and 18:75, before the later contracted past-negative resolution at 18:78.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply the concrete warning and resolution sequence; local form evidence keeps this word as the fuller repeated warning verb.

words.gloss_range: speaker-bound accompaniment condition for the denied capacity
words.root_gloss_range: withness, accompaniment, and co-presence; locally narrowed to an adverbial relation with the speaker, not unrelated heat, roar, or instability branches
words.prose: {{ar:مَعِىَ}} ({{tr:maʿiya}}) is the condition that localizes the denial. Musa is not declared unable to have patience everywhere; the failure is patience with this speaker, inside this companionship. The word carries physical travel together and relational co-witnessing together, because proximity to al-Khiḍr's hidden method is what activates the pressure. A canonical phonological variant shortens the final syllable, making the speaker-bound suffix a pacing point before the final patience noun without changing the companionship meaning. Its recurrence at 18:67 and 18:75 keeps the warning fixed in that companionship, while 2:153 supplies a contrast: withness and patience can be a support formula elsewhere, but here they become the test.

topics.headline: with-me makes the test speaker-specific
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the incapacity is conditioned by being with this speaker, not by patience in the abstract.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the word as an adverbial accompaniment phrase, and the suffix is resolved to the speaker of the rebuke.

topics.headline: companionship is physical and epistemic co-presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the problem is not location alone; shared witnessing of al-Khiḍr's hidden method creates the stress condition for patience.
topics.reason: The local adverbial sense selects accompaniment; the CRITICAL rows validly preserve relational co-witnessing without importing unrelated root branches.

topics.headline: suffix form is also a recitation-sensitive pacing point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker-bound suffix is also where canonical recitation variation affects pacing before the final patience noun, without changing the referent or meaning.
topics.reason: The variant rows are phonological and pacing-oriented; they do not alter the local companionship condition.

topics.headline: companionship-patience relation returns and reverses support formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same companionship condition returns in 18:67 and 18:75, and that the broader with-patience association contrasts with support language at 2:153.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah and cross-surah anchors; local grammar makes this occurrence the condition of denied endurance.

words.gloss_range: bare indefinite verbal noun naming the patience or restraint that cannot be sustained
words.root_gloss_range: self-restraint, endurance, confinement, waiting, and firmness, with many secondary branches; locally narrowed to active self-restraint as the object or specification of denied capacity
words.prose: {{ar:صَبْرًۭا}} ({{tr:ṣabran}}) supplies the final answer to what Musa cannot sustain. As an indefinite verbal noun, it names the discipline of patience itself, without an adjective such as the qualified patience formula at 70:5. The root pressure makes this patience active self-binding, not passive calm; Musa cannot hold himself back under the witnessed acts, and the secondary bitterness image remains a hardship-color rather than a replacement for patience. Across 18:67, 18:72, 18:75, 18:78, and 18:82, this patience is the tested virtue paired with capacity. Because the ayah closes on this noun, the rebuke leaves denied endurance as its final sound and its narrative diagnosis; its indefinite -an cadence also answers the -an close of the previous accusation in 18:71 before the apology of 18:73.

topics.headline: patience names the exact domain of denied capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning is not about all ability; the final noun specifies the ability Musa cannot sustain.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the noun as the accusative complement specifying what cannot be sustained, with object or specification readings both preserving the same local domain.

topics.headline: bare verbal noun makes restraint unqualified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demand is the discipline of patience itself, not an adorned or socially labeled patient identity.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify an indefinite verbal noun with no adjective or construct dependent; the contrast with qualified patience at 70:5 therefore survives.

topics.headline: root image makes patience active self-binding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that patience here is active self-confinement and restraint, while secondary bitterness remains image-pressure rather than replacing the selected meaning.
topics.reason: The local noun means patience or restraint; dictionary evidence supports self-restraint and confinement pressure, while bitter-plant imagery is secondary and therefore only colors the hardship of endurance.

topics.headline: patience is the refrain's tested virtue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that patience and capacity form the controlling pair of the Musa-Khiḍr warning sequence, especially across 18:67, 18:72, 18:75, 18:78, and 18:82.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows show concentration of the capacity-restraint pair in the same narrative, and the local syntax makes this noun the complement of the capacity verb.

topics.headline: final position makes denied endurance the audible takeaway
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on the denied endurance itself, with the prior accusation and next apology framing how that diagnosis is heard.
topics.reason: The closure and cadence rows survive as discourse and sound effects; they do not alter the noun's object or specification role.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Prediction becomes evidence through repetition.** `ق و ل` B001 (“uttered speech”) cites prior speech after the first breach; `ط و ع` B001 again locates failed capacity in companionship. Repetition after 18:67 changes the line from forecast to diagnosed pattern. I infer that the teacher’s reminder is a feedback device: it makes Moses observe his own response, not merely the damaged ship. The lesson’s object begins to include the learner.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:75’s intensified repetition showed the first reminder becoming a progressively personal diagnosis.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Capacity depends on compliance with the learning relation.** `ط و ع/B003` is practical capacity; `ط و ع/B001` is pliant obedience and willing yielding. The same inability predicted in 18:67 returns directly after the question violates 18:70, and 18:73 seeks relief rather than disputing the rule. I infer that `تَسْتَطِيعَ` is not a fixed shortage of temperament: the capacity exists only while the learner yields to the procedure that lets evidence mature. The repeated sentence reads as diagnosis of a relational capability.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:73–76 showed capacity being renegotiated through excuse and a final condition, confirming that it belongs to compliance with the relation.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi beyaz bulutu, yoğun bulutun üzerinde düz duran bulut katmanını ve basamaklar gibi üst üste yığılan bulutları birlikte verir. Çekirdek bulutun beyazlığı ve katmanlı yığılmasıdır; genel yığın yapma eylemi bu dala ancak karşılaştırma düzeyinde yaklaşır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik sınıf çıplak daldır; tanım yalnızca beyaz, düz katmanlı veya üst üste yığılmış bulut anlamını kapsar.
